summary: Franklin County tower near Lonedell: 40 acres acquired for the site in 1949-50, with vandalism reported in 1963, 1964 and 1965. No source gives a build date or its current state.

events.note: vandalism around August 6, 1963: hasp broken off the door and fire finder thrown out of a window; about $25 in damage
vandalism reported in June 1964: windows broken and an electric meter smashed; the vandals were not traced
August 1965: windows, a stool and a fire-finding device broken inside the tower; the youth is named in the source and is not named in the story; he was later fined and sentenced

evidence.supports: Missouri Conservation Commission listing, Franklin County

evidence.quote: 1949-50: 40 acres were acquired for a towersite.

evidence.supports: the 1965 report places the tower two miles east of Lonedell, a Missouri Conservation Commission tower
evidence.quote: at the Missouri Conservation Commission's Forest Fire Lookout Tower, two miles east of Lonedell.

evidence.supports: the tower was vandalized in early August 1963, reported by the district forester
evidence.quote: District Forester John Kullman reports that the Missouri State Conservation Commission fire tower at Lonedell was vandalized sometime Tuesday, August 6.

evidence.supports: the hasp was broken off and the fire finder thrown out of a window in 1963
evidence.quote: The hasp was broken off the door by the vandals and the fire finder was thrown out of the window.
The Conservation Commission reports some vandalism at its Lonedell fire tower one day last week.

evidence.supports: windows broken and an electric meter smashed in 1964
evidence.quote: Windows were broken and an electric meter was smashed, along with slight other damage.

evidence.supports: no trace of the 1964 vandals had been found
evidence.quote: No trace of the vandals has been found.

evidence.supports: August 1965 break-in: windows, a stool and a fire-finding device broken
evidence.quote: broke into the tower and started breaking windows, a stool, and a firefinding device.

evidence.supports: the youth involved was later fined and sentenced
evidence.quote: was fined $100.00, plus court costs, and sentenced to six months in the Franklin county jail

notes_for_editor: One source: the Central US Lookouts Lonedell page. It quotes a 1949-50 state annual report and three Sullivan Tri-County News items (1963, 1964 and 1965). No build date, staffing, height, status or access appears in any source found. The 1965 youth is named in the source; the story leaves him unnamed. The Wikipedia article on Lonedell, linked from the page, does not mention the tower. The 1963 item is dated August 15, 1963 and reports vandalism on August 6. Web search was not available in this run, so no MDC history or newspaper archive was checked.
